options.name: authentication_protocol
options.description: This option allows to configure one of the following authentication protocol types to authenticate the iDRAC user. Secure Hash Algorithm C(SHA). Not applicable for iDRAC10. Message Digest 5 C(MD5). Not applicable for iDRAC10. Secure Hash Algorithm 384-bit C(SHA-384). Only applicable for iDRAC10. Secure Hash Algorithm 512-bit C(SHA-512). Only applicable for iDRAC10. An authentication protocol is not configured if C(None) is selected.

options.name: ca_path
options.description: The Privacy Enhanced Mail (PEM) file that contains a CA certificate to be used for the validation.

options.name: custom_privilege
options.description: The privilege level assigned to the user. Minimum value is 1 for iDRAC10.

options.name: custom_role_name
options.description: custom_role_name is required for iDRAC10 when creating a user using custom role for iDRAC10.

options.name: enable
options.description: Provide the option to enable or disable a user from logging in to iDRAC.

options.name: idrac_ip
options.description: iDRAC IP Address.

options.name: idrac_password
options.description: iDRAC user password. If the password is not provided, then the environment variable E(IDRAC_PASSWORD) is used. Example: export IDRAC_PASSWORD=password

options.name: idrac_port
options.description: iDRAC port.

options.name: idrac_user
options.description: iDRAC username. If the username is not provided, then the environment variable E(IDRAC_USERNAME) is used. Example: export IDRAC_USERNAME=username

options.name: ipmi_lan_privilege
options.description: The Intelligent Platform Management Interface LAN privilege level assigned to the user.

options.name: ipmi_serial_privilege
options.description: The Intelligent Platform Management Interface Serial Port privilege level assigned to the user. This option is only applicable for rack and tower servers.

options.name: new_user_name
options.description: Provide the I(user_name) for the account to be modified.

options.name: privacy_protocol
options.description: This option allows to configure one of the following privacy encryption protocols for the iDRAC user. Data Encryption Standard C(DES). Not applicable for iDRAC10. Advanced Encryption Standard C(AES). Not applicable for iDRAC10. Advanced Encryption Standard 256-bit C(AES-256). Only applicable for iDRAC9 and iDRAC10. A privacy protocol is not configured if C(None) is selected.

options.name: privilege
options.description: Following are the role-based privileges. A user with C(Administrator) privilege can log in to iDRAC, and then configure iDRAC, configure users, clear logs, control and configure system, access virtual console, access virtual media, test alerts, and execute debug commands. A user with C(Operator) privilege can log in to iDRAC, and then configure iDRAC, control and configure system, access virtual console, access virtual media, and execute debug commands. options.name: protocol_enable
options.description: Enables protocol for the iDRAC user.

options.name: sol_enable
options.description: Enables Serial Over Lan (SOL) for an iDRAC user.

options.name: state
options.description: Select C(present) to create or modify a user account. Select C(absent) to remove a user account.

options.name: timeout
options.description: The socket level timeout in seconds.

options.name: user_name
options.description: Provide the I(user_name) of the account to be created, deleted or modified.

options.name: user_password
options.description: Provide the password for the user account. The password can be changed when the user account is modified. To ensure security, the I(user_password) must be at least eight characters long and must contain lowercase and upper-case characters, numbers, and special characters.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: If C(false), the SSL certificates will not be validated. Configure C(false) only on personally controlled sites where self-signed certificates are used. Prior to collection version C(5.0.0), the I(validate_certs) is C(false) by default.

options.name: x_auth_token
options.description: Authentication token. If the x_auth_token is not provided, then the environment variable E(IDRAC_X_AUTH_TOKEN) is used. Example: export IDRAC_X_AUTH_TOKEN=x_auth_token
